t: Buddhism grew from the teaching of Siddhartha Gautama, the Buddha, in north-east India in the 5th century BCE: suffering arises from craving, and a path of ethics, meditation and insight leads to its end.
Royal patrons such as Ashoka, monks and merchants carried it to Sri Lanka, Central Asia, China, Korea, Japan, Tibet and Southeast Asia, where it took the Theravada, Mahayana and Vajrayana forms.
It faded from India after about 1200 but remained a major religion of Asia, was revived in India by B. R. Ambedkar in 1956 and reached Europe and the Americas in the 20th century.
dyk: The oldest printed book that bears a date is a Buddhist scripture: a copy of the Diamond Sutra, printed in China in 868 and found in a sealed cave at Dunhuang in 1900.
ev: Siddhartha Gautama attains awakening at Bodh Gaya and gives his first teaching at Sarnath
The Mauryan emperor Ashoka turns to the Buddha’s teaching and promotes it across his empire
The Pali Canon is written down in Sri Lanka, by tradition at the Aluvihara monastery
Buddhism reaches China along the trade routes of Central Asia
Buddhism is brought to Japan from the Korean kingdom of Baekje
Samye, the first Buddhist monastery in Tibet, is consecrated
The great monastery of Nalanda is sacked, and Buddhism fades from most of India
B. R. Ambedkar and hundreds of thousands of his followers become Buddhists at Nagpur

f.origin: The Ganges plain of north-east India (Magadha and Kosala), 5th century BCE
f.scriptures: The Pali Canon (Tipitaka); the Mahayana sutras; the Tibetan Kangyur and Tengyur
f.followers: Several hundred million: estimates range from about 320 to 500 million, depending on how practice in East Asia is counted
